notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1786). Words follow the engraving's spelling (quì, sò, sà beside sa, nò, si for sì, sù, giacche for giacchè, briaco, gittar, veggio, gito, poc' anzi, chi'l, cos' hai, all' erta, quest' è, sugello, sussurro, diventasti and fosti where the libretto has diventaste and foste, 'or ci forse sarà' where the libretto has 'ov'ei forse sarà', 'Perchè fare?' for 'Per che fare?'). The opening sir./rir. are the tied last syllables of desir and comparir carried over from the preceding section. IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, elisions (two words on one note in the score) joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ, intervocalic s voiced (cosa, così, rinchiuso, l'usanza), gn and gli held double (siɲˈɲor, biʎˈʎet.to), nasal assimilation within words (ˈduŋ.kwe, riŋˈkju.zo, iɱˈva.no), z as [ts] (insolenza, pazienza, pazzo, zitto); sugello is sung with a double g (suggello), di' in 'di su' is the imperative of dire. Translation literal, for meaning.
